title: How Machines Learn Your Brain Code
hook: A drop of fruit juice in 1969 created the first brain-computer interface.
script: A drop of fruit juice in 1969 created the first brain-computer interface. Could direct thought control actually let paralyzed patients speak through machines? Reading brainwaves using non-invasive EEG is like recording a whisper from outside a packed stadium. Implanted sensors bypass this noise by measuring single voltage spikes from potassium ions. In modern trials, paralyzed patients reached sixty-two words per minute with astonishing precision. But the machine does not learn you; your brain alters its own code to match the device. Your nervous system rewires itself just to feed the machine its next drop.
